correctness.rationale: The support curvature is positive for |epsilon|<=1/4 by a direct Hessian Frobenius bound. The previously published pointwise brightness formula is correctly treated as a premise. Uniform spherical coordinates reduce Y exactly to A(S)+B(S)sin²(2Phi), where S uniform and the angle term beta-half. This proves the CDF and density. A complete Lagrange-multiplier critical census gives six minima, twelve saddles, eight maxima; the saddle quadratic form w²/4-alpha² and Haar Jacobian fix 6/pi as the exact two-sided log coefficient. Cap expansions prove endpoint slopes and Dirichlet monomial evaluation yields the rational moments. The independently executed embedded Python reproduces moments and numeric singular behavior; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The full Haar law for a natural tetrahedrally symmetric constant-width body distinguishes its projection-area statistics from a previously evaluated rotationally symmetric cubic. Twelve Morse saddles produce an interior logarithmic density transition with a precise universal coefficient, and six/eight extremal points yield sharp endpoint slopes. A fully specified one-dimensional arcsine mixture and rational first two moments give reproducible geometric-probability benchmarks. This is more than a renaming or trivial parametric substitution.
